rules.sentence: As a corollary of its vastly superior contrast resolution for soft tissues, CT has a far higher sensitivity for the diagnosis of infectious spondylodiscitis.
CT is superior even to MRI in visualizing both the sequestra and the subsequent calcifications; the latter points towards tuberculous spondylodiscitis.
The reduction in density of the intervertebral disc can be visualized in very early stages, as well as the thinning of the paravertebral fat.
Bone destruction and sequestra formation can be seen in later stages.
Moreover, the extension of the inflammation can be seen clearly, along with potential abscesses and epidural phlegmons, causing spinal cord compression.
